pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Easy, Simple, Moderate, Difficult, Hard, Challenging…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words describe different difficulty levels in Japanese. You can use them to talk about tasks, tests, or situations that are easy or hard.

examples.target: このテストはやさしいです。
examples.english: This test is easy.

examples.target: かんたんな問題をください。
examples.english: Please give me simple questions.

examples.target: この仕事はちゅうくらいのむずかしさです。
examples.english: This job has a moderate difficulty.

examples.target: むずかしい本を読みます。
examples.english: I read a difficult book.

examples.target: たいへんな仕事をしました。
examples.english: I did a hard job.

examples.target: ふくざつな問題を解きます。
examples.english: I solve complicated problems.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Cleanser, Toner, Serum, Essence, Moisturizer, Eye Cream…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common skincare products in Japanese. You can use these words to talk about your daily skincare routine or when shopping for beauty products in Japan.

examples.target: 毎朝、クレンザーで顔を洗います。
examples.english: Every morning, I wash my face with a cleanser.

examples.target: トナーを使って肌を整えます。
examples.english: I use toner to prepare my skin.

examples.target: セラムは肌に栄養を与えます。
examples.english: Serum gives nutrients to the skin.

examples.target: 保湿クリームを塗って乾燥を防ぎます。
examples.english: I apply moisturizer to prevent dryness.

examples.target: 日焼け止めを塗って外に出ます。
examples.english: I put on sunscreen before going outside.

examples.target: 夜にフェイスマスクを使います。
examples.english: I use a face mask at night.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Boredom, Interest, Curiosity, Hobby, Passion, Interest in something…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: This vocabulary theme covers feelings related to boredom and interest. You can use these words to talk about what you like, what fascinates you, or when you feel bored. They are useful for expressing emotions and hobbies in daily conversations.

examples.target: 今日は退屈です。
examples.english: I am bored today.

examples.target: 私は音楽に興味があります。
examples.english: I am interested in music.

examples.target: 新しい趣味を始めました。
examples.english: I started a new hobby.

examples.target: 彼女は好奇心が強いです。
examples.english: She has strong curiosity.

examples.target: 彼の情熱はサッカーです。
examples.english: His passion is soccer.

examples.target: この本の魅力は面白い話です。
examples.english: The fascination of this book is its interesting story.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Ramen, Black bean noodles, Spicy seafood noodles, Cold noodles, Udon, Soba…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: This vocabulary theme introduces different types of noodles in Japanese. You can use these words when ordering food or talking about your favorite dishes in Japan.

examples.target: 私はラーメンが好きです。
examples.english: I like ramen.

examples.target: 冷やし中華は夏に食べます。
examples.english: I eat cold noodles in summer.

examples.target: うどんは太くて柔らかいです。
examples.english: Udon is thick and soft.

examples.target: そばは健康にいいです。
examples.english: Soba is good for your health.

examples.target: ジャージャー麺は黒いソースがあります。
examples.english: Black bean noodles have a black sauce.

examples.target: 春雨は透明で細い麺です。
examples.english: Glass noodles are transparent and thin.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Bed, Pillow, Blanket, Closet, Desk, Chair…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common words for items you find in a bedroom. Use them to talk about your room or describe where things are. For example, you can say where the bed or lamp is in your room.

examples.target: ベッドの上にまくらがあります。
examples.english: There is a pillow on the bed.

examples.target: もうふはあたたかいです。
examples.english: The blanket is warm.

examples.target: つくえの上にランプがあります。
examples.english: There is a lamp on the desk.

examples.target: いすはつくえのそばにあります。
examples.english: The chair is next to the desk.

examples.target: おしいれの中にふとんがあります。
examples.english: There is a futon in the closet.

examples.target: まどのそばにじゅうたんがあります。
examples.english: There is a rug near the window.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Bus, Bus Stop, Fare Card, Bus Fare, Get On, Get Off…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: This vocabulary theme helps you talk about buses and public transit in Japanese. You can use these words to ask about bus stops, fares, and how to get on or off the bus.

examples.target: バス停はどこですか？
examples.english: Where is the bus stop?

examples.target: 次の停留所で降ります。
examples.english: I will get off at the next stop.

examples.target: 乗車カードで運賃を払います。
examples.english: I pay the bus fare with a fare card.

examples.target: この路線のバスに乗ります。
examples.english: I will get on the bus of this route.

examples.target: 優先席はあそこです。
examples.english: The priority seats are over there.

words.english: What do you like to do?
words.target: 何をするのが好きですか？
words.romanization: Nani o suru no ga suki desu ka?

words.target: 美味しい食べ物は好きですか？
words.romanization: Oishii tabemono wa suki desu ka?

words.target: どこか面白いところに旅行しましたか？
words.romanization: Doko ka omoshiroi tokoro ni ryokō shimashita ka?

words.english: Do you watch movies or dramas?
words.target: 映画やドラマを見ますか？
words.romanization: Eiga ya dorama o mimasu ka?

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Nice to meet you., What do you like to do?, Where are you from?, How’s your week going?, What’s the weather like?, Do you like good food?…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These phrases are useful for starting small talk in Japanese. Use them to ask simple questions and get to know someone in a friendly way.

examples.target: はじめまして。よろしくお願いします。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. Please treat me well.

examples.target: どこから来ましたか？
examples.english: Where are you from?

examples.target: 今週はどうですか？
examples.english: How’s your week going?

examples.target: 美味しい食べ物は好きですか？
examples.english: Do you like good food?

examples.target: 映画やドラマを見ますか？
examples.english: Do you watch movies or dramas?

examples.target: ペットはいますか？
examples.english: Do you have any pets?

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: What?, When?, Where?, Who?, Why?, How?…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common question words in Japanese used to ask for information. You can use them to ask about things, time, places, people, reasons, methods, prices, and quantities.

examples.target: これは何？
examples.english: What is this?

examples.target: あなたはいつ来ますか？
examples.english: When will you come?

examples.target: 駅はどこですか？
examples.english: Where is the station?

examples.target: だれが先生ですか？
examples.english: Who is the teacher?

examples.target: なぜ勉強しますか？
examples.english: Why do you study?

examples.target: これはいくらですか？
examples.english: How much is this?

words.target: もう一度言ってください。
どうもありがとうございます。

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Excuse me, Pardon?, I can't hear well., I'm sorry., It's my fault., Could you repeat that?…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common Japanese phrases you can use to get someone's attention, ask for clarification, or apologize politely. They are useful in everyday situations when you need help or want to be polite.

examples.target: すみません、もう一度言ってください。
examples.english: Excuse me, could you repeat that?

examples.target: よく聞こえません。もう一度お願いします。
examples.english: I can't hear well. Please say it again.

examples.target: なんですか？
examples.english: Pardon?

examples.target: 道に迷いました。どこですか？
examples.english: I'm lost. Where is it?

examples.target: ごめんなさい。私のせいです。
examples.english: I'm sorry. It's my fault.

examples.target: どうもありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you so much.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Hot, Warm, Mild, Cool, Chilly, Cold…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words describe different temperatures and weather conditions in Japanese. Use them to talk about how hot or cold something is, or to describe the weather outside.

examples.target: 今日はとてもあついです。
examples.english: Today is very hot.

examples.target: この部屋はあたたかいです。
examples.english: This room is warm.

examples.target: すずしい風がふいています。
examples.english: A cool breeze is blowing.

examples.target: さむいからコートを着てください。
examples.english: It's cold, so please wear a coat.

examples.target: こおりの上を歩くのは危ないです。
examples.english: Walking on ice is dangerous.

examples.target: きびしいさむさで外に出たくないです。
examples.english: I don't want to go outside because of the frigid cold.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Fragrant, Aromatic, Stinky, Fishy, Cheesy, Musty…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words describe different smells you might notice in everyday life. You can use them to talk about pleasant or unpleasant odors around you.

examples.target: この花はいい香りがします。
examples.english: This flower has a fragrant smell.

examples.target: チーズのにおいが部屋にあります。
examples.english: There is a cheesy smell in the room.

examples.target: 魚くさい魚を食べたくないです。
examples.english: I don't want to eat fish that smells fishy.

examples.target: かびくさい部屋は掃除が必要です。
examples.english: A musty room needs cleaning.

examples.target: 煙い空気は体に良くないです。
examples.english: Smoky air is not good for your body.

examples.target: このチーズは刺激的なにおいがします。
examples.english: This cheese has a pungent smell.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Run, Swim, Shoot, Pass, Hit, Lift…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common sports action verbs in Japanese. You can use them to talk about playing sports, exercising, or moving your body during activities.

examples.target: 毎朝公園で走る。
examples.english: I run in the park every morning.

examples.target: プールで泳ぐのが好きです。
examples.english: I like swimming in the pool.

examples.target: サッカーでボールをパスする。
examples.english: I pass the ball in soccer.

examples.target: 彼はボールをシュートした。
examples.english: He shot the ball.

examples.target: バットでボールを打つ。
examples.english: I hit the ball with a bat.

examples.target: ジャンプしてボールをキャッチする。
examples.english: I jump and catch the ball.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Pencil, Eraser, Sketchbook, Watercolor, Paintbrush, Acrylic Paint…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common art supplies you can use when drawing or painting. Knowing these words helps you talk about your art tools in Japanese and follow instructions for art projects.

examples.target: えんぴつでえをかきます。
examples.english: I draw a picture with a pencil.

examples.target: けしごむでまちがいをけします。
examples.english: I erase mistakes with an eraser.

examples.target: スケッチブックにスケッチをします。
examples.english: I make sketches in my sketchbook.

examples.target: ふでとみずえのぐをつかいます。
examples.english: I use a paintbrush and watercolor.

examples.target: はさみでかみをきります。
examples.english: I cut paper with scissors.

examples.target: のりスティックでかみをはります。
examples.english: I stick paper with a glue stick.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Compassion, Kindness, Understanding, Support, Care, Sincerity…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words help you talk about feelings and actions that show care and respect for others. Use them to describe how you understand and support people in kind and thoughtful ways.

examples.target: 彼はいつも親切で、友達を助けます。
examples.english: He is always kind and helps his friends.

examples.target: 思いやりのある言葉は人を元気にします。
examples.english: Compassionate words cheer people up.

examples.target: 私は友達の気持ちを理解しています。
examples.english: I understand my friend's feelings.

examples.target: 支援が必要な時は、声をかけてください。
examples.english: Please ask for support when you need it.

examples.target: 彼女は誠実で、いつも正直です。
examples.english: She is sincere and always honest.

examples.target: 尊敬は良い人間関係の基本です。
examples.english: Respect is the foundation of good relationships.

words.target: アイボリー / フェア

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Ivory / Fair, Beige, Natural Beige, Tan, Brown, Pink…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words are common makeup shade names in Japanese, often used when choosing foundation or lipstick colors. They are mostly borrowed from English and written in katakana. Use them to describe or ask about makeup colors.

examples.target: このファンデーションはナチュラルベージュです。
examples.english: This foundation is natural beige.

examples.target: ピンクのリップが好きです。
examples.english: I like pink lipstick.

examples.target: アイボリーの色は肌に合います。
examples.english: Ivory color suits my skin.

examples.target: ブラウンのアイシャドウを使います。
examples.english: I use brown eyeshadow.

examples.target: コーラルのチークを買いました。
examples.english: I bought coral blush.

examples.target: モーブの口紅を試してください。
examples.english: Please try the mauve lipstick.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: in, inside, on, on top of, under, below, next to, beside, in front of, before, behind, at the back of…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words help you describe the position of objects or people in Japanese. Use them to say where something is located, like 'on the table' or 'next to the chair.' They are very useful in daily conversation.

examples.target: ねこはいすのうえにいます。
examples.english: The cat is on the chair.

examples.target: ほんはつくえのしたにあります。
examples.english: The book is under the desk.

examples.target: いぬはへやのなかにいます。
examples.english: The dog is inside the room.

examples.target: がっこうはこうえんのまえにあります。
examples.english: The school is in front of the park.

examples.target: つくえはいすのとなりにあります。
examples.english: The desk is next to the chair.

examples.target: かばんはつくえといすのあいだにあります。
examples.english: The bag is between the desk and the chair.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Wow, What?!, No way!, Seriously?!, Oh my!, Oh no!…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These expressions are used to show surprise or shock in Japanese. You can use them when something unexpected happens or when you are amazed or upset by news or events.

examples.target: わあ、きれいな花ですね！
examples.english: Wow, what beautiful flowers!

examples.target: えっ？！本当ですか？
examples.english: What?! Is that true?

examples.target: まさか、彼が来るとは思わなかった。
examples.english: No way, I didn't think he would come.

examples.target: びっくりした！犬が急に走った。
examples.english: What a surprise! The dog suddenly ran.

examples.target: いやだ！宿題を忘れた。
examples.english: Oh no! I forgot my homework.

examples.target: 信じられない！あの映画は本当に面白かった。
examples.english: I can't believe it! That movie was really interesting.

words.target: サービス料は含まれていますか？

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Tax, Tax rate, Value-added tax (VAT), Tax amount, Total (including tax), Tip…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These words help you understand and talk about taxes and tips when you pay in Japan. Use them to ask about prices, tax amounts, or whether you should leave a tip.

examples.target: この商品の税込み合計はいくらですか？
examples.english: What is the total price including tax for this product?

examples.target: 消費税は今１０パーセントです。
examples.english: The value-added tax is 10% now.

examples.target: サービス料は含まれていますか？
examples.english: Is the service charge included?

examples.target: チップは不要です。
examples.english: No tip is needed.

examples.target: レストランでチップを渡します。
examples.english: I will leave a tip at the restaurant.

examples.target: 税金と税率について教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me about tax and tax rate.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Apple, Pear, Grape, Peach, Persimmon, Plum…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common fruits in Japanese. You can use these words to talk about your favorite fruits or to buy fruits at a market or store.

examples.target: りんごが好きです。
examples.english: I like apples.

examples.target: みかんを食べます。
examples.english: I eat an orange.

examples.target: いちごはあまいです。
examples.english: Strawberries are sweet.

examples.target: スーパーでぶどうを買います。
examples.english: I buy grapes at the supermarket.

examples.target: かきを食べました。
examples.english: I ate a persimmon.

examples.target: ももとなしがあります。
examples.english: There are peaches and pears.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Cabbage, Spinach, Lettuce, Basil leaves, Parsley, Bok choy…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common vegetables in Japanese, often used in cooking and salads. You can use these words to talk about ingredients or ask for vegetables at a market or restaurant.

examples.target: サラダにレタスとトマトを入れます。
examples.english: I put lettuce and tomatoes in the salad.

examples.target: スーパーでキャベツを買いました。
examples.english: I bought cabbage at the supermarket.

examples.target: ほうれん草は栄養がたくさんあります。
examples.english: Spinach has a lot of nutrients.

examples.target: バジルの葉をパスタに使います。
examples.english: I use basil leaves in pasta.

examples.target: チンゲンサイは中華料理によく使います。
examples.english: Bok choy is often used in Chinese cooking.

examples.target: パセリを料理の飾りにします。
examples.english: I use parsley as a garnish for dishes.

examples.target: わたしはクラスでにばんめです。
examples.english: I am second in the class.

examples.target: このほんはさんばんめにおもしろいです。
examples.english: This book is the third most interesting.

examples.target: しゅくだいはよんばんめにやります。
examples.english: I will do the homework fourth.

examples.target: レースでろくばんめになりました。
examples.english: I came in sixth in the race.

examples.target: パーティーははちばんめのへやであります。
examples.english: The party is in the eighth room.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: My name, My age, My country, My hometown, My job, My hobby…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These phrases help you introduce yourself in Japanese. Use them to talk about your name, age, country, and other personal details when meeting new people. Start conversations with はじめまして (Nice to meet you).

examples.target: はじめまして。わたしのなまえはケンです。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. My name is Ken.

examples.target: わたしのとしはにじゅうごさいです。
examples.english: I am 25 years old.

examples.target: わたしのくにはアメリカです。
examples.english: My country is the United States.

examples.target: わたしのしゅっしんはとうきょうです。
examples.english: My hometown is Tokyo.

examples.target: わたしのしごとはせんせいです。
examples.english: My job is a teacher.

examples.target: わたしのしゅみはサッカーです。
examples.english: My hobby is soccer.

pages.description: Learn Japanese vocabulary: Basil, Mint, Rosemary, Cilantro, Garlic, Ginger…. Save-friendly chart with pronunciation.
pages.explanationEn: These are common herbs and spices used in cooking. You can use them to talk about flavors or ingredients in Japanese recipes.

examples.target: にんにくを料理に入れます。
examples.english: I put garlic in the dish.

examples.target: ミントはお茶に使います。
examples.english: Mint is used in tea.

examples.target: こしょうを少しください。
examples.english: Please give me a little black pepper.

examples.target: チリは辛いです。
examples.english: Chili is spicy.

examples.target: しょうがは体にいいです。
examples.english: Ginger is good for your health.

examples.target: バジルとローズマリーはハーブです。
examples.english: Basil and rosemary are herbs.

Eye colors in Korean: black, brown, hazel, green, blue, gray….

pages.description: Months in Korean: January, February, March, April, May, June….

examples.target: 오월은 봄이에요.

pages.description: Emotions in Korean: happy, sad, angry, tired, surprised, scared….

examples.target: 나는 오늘 행복해요.
examples.english: I am happy today.

examples.target: 그 영화가 슬펐어요.
examples.english: That movie was sad.

pages.titleEn: How to check in at a goshiwon in Korean
pages.description: First Day at a Goshiwon. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: First Day at a Goshiwon

lines.ko: 오늘은 내가 고시원에서 첫날을 보냈어요.
lines.en: Today was my first day at the goshiwon.

lines.ko: 방이 아주 작지만 필요한 게 다 있어요.
lines.en: The room is very small but has everything I need.

lines.ko: 공용 주방이 있어서 간단히 밥을 해 먹었어요.
lines.en: There is a shared kitchen, so I cooked a simple meal.

lines.ko: 처음에 옆 방에서 큰 소리가 나서 놀랐어요.
lines.en: At first, I was surprised by loud noise from the next room.

lines.ko: 하지만 금방 조용해져서 잘 수 있었어요.
lines.en: But soon it got quiet, so I could sleep well.

lines.ko: 내일은 사장님과 계약서에 대해 이야기할 거예요.
lines.en: Tomorrow, I will talk with the owner about the contract.

lines.ko: 혼자 사는 게 처음이라 조금 긴장되지만 기대돼요.
lines.en: Living alone for the first time makes me nervous but excited.

pages.titleEn: How to move into a goshiwon in Korean
pages.description: First Day at a Korean Goshiwon. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: First Day at a Korean Goshiwon

lines.ko: 오늘부터 고시원에서 살기 시작했어요.
lines.en: Today, I started living in a goshiwon.

lines.ko: 방은 아주 작지만 창문이 있어서 좋아요.
lines.en: The room is very small, but I like that it has a window.

lines.ko: 처음에는 조용한 환경이 조금 낯설었어요.
lines.en: At first, the quiet environment felt a bit unfamiliar.

lines.ko: 옆방에서 공부하는 소리가 들려서 집중돼요.
lines.en: I can hear studying sounds from the next room, so I can focus.

lines.ko: 고시원 주인 아주머니가 친절하게 인사했어요.
lines.en: The goshiwon owner's aunt greeted me kindly.

lines.ko: 자취할 때보다 생활비가 훨씬 절약될 것 같아요.
lines.en: I think I'll save much more on living expenses than when living alone.

lines.ko: 내일부터는 규칙적으로 생활하려고 노력할 거예요.
lines.en: Starting tomorrow, I'll try to live more regularly.

lines.ko: 조금 외롭지만 새로운 시작이라서 기대돼요.
lines.en: I feel a little lonely, but I'm excited about this new beginning.

reading.sceneEn: First Day at a Korean Goshiwon

pages.titleEn: How to use a PC bang in Korean

lines.ko: 오늘은 친구와 처음으로 PC방에 갔어요.

lines.ko: 컴퓨터가 빠르고 게임 화면이 정말 선명했어요.
lines.en: The computer was fast and the game screen was really clear.

lines.ko: 처음 해보는 게임이라 조금 어렵게 느껴졌어요.
lines.en: Since it was my first time playing the game, it felt a bit difficult.

lines.ko: 친구가 친절하게 게임 방법을 가르쳐 주었어요.
lines.en: My friend kindly taught me how to play the game.

lines.ko: 음료수와 간식을 주문해서 먹으면서 즐거웠어요.
lines.en: We ordered drinks and snacks and enjoyed eating them.

lines.ko: 시간 가는 줄 모르고 게임을 계속했어요.
lines.en: I kept playing the game without noticing the time.

lines.ko: PC방이 이렇게 편리하고 재미있을 줄 몰랐어요.
lines.en: I didn’t know PC bangs could be so convenient and fun.

lines.ko: 다음에도 친구들과 함께 PC방에 또 가고 싶어요.
lines.en: I want to go to the PC bang again with my friends next time.

reading.sceneEn: First Time at a PC Bang

pages.titleEn: How to order fried chicken in Korean
pages.description: First Time Ordering Korean Fried Chicken. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: First Time Ordering Korean Fried Chicken

lines.ko: 오늘 처음으로 한국에서 치킨을 시켜 봤어요.
lines.en: Today, I ordered Korean fried chicken for the first time.

lines.ko: 인터넷에서 메뉴를 검색했는데 종류가 정말 많더라고요.
lines.en: I searched the menu online, and there were so many kinds.

lines.ko: 골뱅이 무침도 같이 먹고 싶었지만 무거워서 그냥 치킨만 시켰어요.
lines.en: I wanted to eat spicy whelk salad too, but it was too heavy, so I only ordered chicken.

lines.ko: 배달 앱으로 주소를 입력하는 데 어려움이 조금 있었어요.
lines.en: I had a little trouble entering my address on the delivery app.

lines.ko: 시킨 치킨이 빨리 왔으면 좋겠다고 계속 생각했어요.
lines.en: I kept hoping the chicken would arrive soon.

lines.ko: 드디어 배달원이 초인종을 눌러서 문을 열었어요.
lines.en: Finally, the delivery person rang the doorbell and I opened the door.

lines.ko: 치킨 포장 용기가 뜨거워서 조심해서 집 안으로 들어왔어요.
lines.en: The chicken container was hot, so I carefully brought it inside.

lines.ko: 먹어 보니까 정말 바삭하고 양념이 맛있었어요.
lines.en: When I ate it, it was really crispy and the sauce was delicious.

lines.ko: 다음에도 꼭 치킨을 시켜 먹을 거예요.
lines.en: I will definitely order fried chicken again next time.

reading.sceneEn: First Time Ordering Korean Fried Chicken

pages.titleEn: How to use a jjimjilbang in Korean
pages.description: First Time Using a Korean Public Bath. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: First Time Using a Korean Public Bath

lines.ko: 오늘은 한국 찜질방에 처음 가보는 날이에요.
lines.en: Today is the first day I'm going to a Korean public bath.

lines.ko: 들어가자마자 뜨거운 물이 정말 인상적이었어요.
lines.en: As soon as I entered, the hot water was really impressive.

lines.ko: 사우나 방은 너무 더워서 잠시만 있어도 땀이 났어요.
lines.en: The sauna room was so hot that I started sweating just by staying a moment.

lines.ko: 찜질방에서 먹는 식혜가 이렇게 맛있는 줄 몰랐어요.
lines.en: I didn't know that the sweet rice drink here tastes this good.

lines.ko: 다른 사람들과 같이 누워서 쉬는 시간이 참 편안했어요.
lines.en: Lying down and resting with other people was really comfortable.

lines.ko: 처음에는 조금 긴장했지만 금방 적응할 수 있었어요.
lines.en: At first, I was a bit nervous but I quickly got used to it.

lines.ko: 한국 찜질방 문화가 이렇게 특별한지 알게 되어 기뻤어요.
lines.en: I'm glad I learned how special the Korean public bath culture is.

reading.sceneEn: First Time Using a Korean Public Bath

pages.titleEn: How to use a public bathhouse in Korean
pages.description: First Time Using a Public Bathhouse. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: First Time Using a Public Bathhouse

lines.ko: 저는 어제 친구들과 함께 처음으로 공중목욕탕에 갔어요.
lines.en: Yesterday, I went to a public bathhouse for the first time with my friends.

lines.ko: 처음 가보는 곳이라 조금 긴장됐어요.
lines.en: I was a bit nervous because it was my first time going there.

lines.ko: 입구에서 신발을 벗고 사물함 열쇠를 받았어요.
lines.en: At the entrance, I took off my shoes and got a locker key.

lines.ko: 사물함에 옷을 넣고 목욕탕으로 들어갔어요.
lines.en: I put my clothes in the locker and went into the bathhouse.

lines.ko: 처음에는 찬물도 있고 따뜻한 물도 있어서 놀랐어요.
lines.en: At first, I was surprised because there was both cold and warm water.

lines.ko: 몸을 깨끗이 씻는 공간이 따로 있더라고요.
lines.en: There was a separate area to wash your body thoroughly.

lines.ko: 친구가 씻는 방법을 알려줘서 잘 따라했어요.
lines.en: My friend showed me how to wash properly, so I followed well.

lines.ko: 그리고 따뜻한 욕조에 들어가서 정말 편안했어요.
lines.en: Then I got into the warm bath, and it was really relaxing.

lines.ko: 목욕 후에는 휴게실에서 음료수를 마셨어요.
lines.en: After the bath, I drank a beverage in the resting area.

lines.ko: 공중목욕탕이 이렇게 좋은 곳인지 몰랐어요.
lines.en: I didn’t know that public bathhouses were such nice places.

lines.ko: 친구들과 이야기하면서 새로운 문화를 경험해서 기뻤어요.
lines.en: I was happy to experience a new culture while talking with my friends.

lines.ko: 다음에도 꼭 또 가고 싶어요.
lines.en: I definitely want to go again next time.

lines.ko: 처음이라 조금 어색했지만 이제는 익숙해졌어요.
lines.en: It was a little awkward at first, but now I’m used to it.

lines.ko: 공중목욕탕에서 만난 다른 사람들도 친절했어요.
lines.en: The other people I met at the bathhouse were also kind.

reading.sceneEn: First Time Using a Public Bathhouse

pages.titleEn: How to order at a convenience store in Korean
pages.description: Ordering at a convenience store late at night. Korean audio story — listen on the website.
pages.explanationEn: Ordering at a convenience store late at night

lines.ko: 안녕하세요! 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
lines.en: Hello! How can I help you?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 아이스 아메리카노 하나 주세요.
lines.en: Hello. I'd like one iced americano, please.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.ko: 사이즈는 어떻게 드릴까요?
lines.en: What size would you like?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.ko: 제일 큰 사이즈로 주세요. 얼음은 조금만 넣어 주세요.
lines.en: The biggest size, please. Please put only a little ice.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.ko: 네, 알겠습니다. 그리고 다른 음료도 필요하세요?
lines.en: Okay, got it. Do you need any other drinks?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.ko: 아니요, 아이스 아메리카노 하나면 충분해요. 계산해 주세요.
lines.en: No, one iced americano is enough. Please ring me up.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.ko: 총 4,000원입니다. 카드로 결제하시겠어요?
lines.en: That will be 4,000 won. Would you like to pay by card?
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.ko: 네, 카드로 결제할게요. 감사합니다.
lines.en: Yes, I'll pay by card. Thank you.
lines.speaker: Customer

lines.ko: 감사합니다! 좋은 하루 보내세요!
lines.en: Thank you! Have a nice day!
lines.speaker: Clerk

reading.sceneEn: Ordering at a convenience store late at night

pages.titleEn: How to talk at a pharmacy in Korean
pages.description: Pharmacy conversation in Korean. Listen sentence by sentence.
pages.explanationEn: Pharmacy conversation in Korean

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.ko: 어서 오세요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
lines.en: Welcome. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.ko: 두통약 있어요?
lines.en: Do you have headache medicine?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.ko: 네, 있어요. 이 약이 좋아요.
lines.en: Yes, we do. This medicine is good.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.ko: 어떻게 먹어요?
lines.en: How do I take it?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.ko: 하루에 두 번, 식후에 드세요.
lines.en: Take it twice a day, after meals.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.ko: 얼마예요?
lines.en: How much is it?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.ko: 5,000원입니다.
lines.en: It's 5,000 won.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.ko: 주세요. 감사합니다.
lines.en: Please give it to me. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.ko: 네, 감사합니다.
lines.en: Yes, thank you.
